title: ChatGPT Fundamentals
description: ChatGPT feels magical — but it is not. This lesson explains what ChatGPT actually is, what it is good at, and the most important limitation you need to know.
learningObjectives: Explain what ChatGPT is and what GPT means
Identify the types of tasks ChatGPT does well
Recognize hallucinations and why they happen
Know when to trust and when to verify ChatGPT's output

opening.hook: You have probably asked ChatGPT a question and gotten a very convincing answer — that turned out to be wrong. It happens to everyone. But why does it happen? And how can you use ChatGPT without being misled?
opening.relevance: Understanding ChatGPT's design helps you use it effectively without being fooled by confident-sounding errors.

content.content: ChatGPT is a conversational AI system developed by OpenAI. It is built on top of a family of large language models — GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o — that have been fine-tuned to follow instructions and hold conversations.

content.definition: Generative Pre-trained Transformer — a type of large language model architecture.
content.example: GPT-4 is the model behind one version of ChatGPT. GPT-4o is a more recent multimodal model.

content.title: What ChatGPT does NOT do
content.content: ChatGPT does not search a database for the right answer. It generates text by predicting the most likely sequence of words based on patterns learned during training. This is why it can produce confident-sounding statements that are completely false.
ChatGPT excels at a specific set of tasks. Recognizing them helps you use it well.

content.title: ChatGPT is good at:
items: Explaining concepts — anything from quantum physics to contract law
Brainstorming — generating ideas for projects, names, strategies
Writing code — generating, debugging, and explaining code
Answering questions — within the limits of its training data

content.title: ChatGPT in a real workflow
steps: Prompt: 'Write a polite email to a client explaining a 3-day delay. Keep it under 100 words.'
Human edit: Review for tone, accuracy, context
Result: Email completed in 30 seconds instead of 10 minutes

content.content: ChatGPT's biggest weakness is hallucination. This is when the model produces information that sounds plausible but is factually wrong — invented facts, made-up citations, fake statistics.

content.definition: When an AI model generates plausible-sounding but false information.
content.example: ChatGPT might invent a court case that does not exist, or misattribute a quote to the wrong person.

content.title: Why hallucinations happen
content.content: ChatGPT predicts the most likely next word. If a false statement sounds plausible — if it 'feels' like something a lawyer or scientist might say — the model generates it. It has no built-in check against reality.

content.before: What people expect: ChatGPT either knows or doesn't know.
content.after: What actually happens: ChatGPT always generates an answer — correct or not — with equal confidence.

content.title: How to protect yourself
items: Always verify important facts, citations, and statistics
Ask ChatGPT to cite sources — then check the sources
Treat ChatGPT as a first-draft assistant, not an oracle
When accuracy matters, use search-augmented tools or verify externally

content.myth: ChatGPT is right most of the time — I can trust it.
content.reality: ChatGPT is useful most of the time. But 'useful' and 'correct' are different. Always verify factual claims.

keyTakeaways: ChatGPT is a conversational AI built on GPT models.
It generates text — it does not retrieve facts from a database.
It excels at drafting, explaining, brainstorming, translating, and coding.
Its biggest weakness is hallucination — confident but false information.

reflection.prompt: Think of a situation where you might have trusted ChatGPT too much. What would you do differently now?
reflection.hint: Consider: facts, citations, legal or medical advice, statistics.
reflection.expectedInsight: ChatGPT is a tool, not an authority. Verification is part of using it responsibly.

flashcards.front: Does ChatGPT search a database for answers?
flashcards.back: No — it generates text by predicting the most likely sequence of words.
When a model generates plausible-sounding but false information.
Drafting, explaining, brainstorming, translating, coding, answering questions.
Because it predicts plausible text — not factual text. It has no reality check.

items.question: Why can ChatGPT produce confident-sounding false information?
options: It generates plausible text, not factual text
It has a bug in the fact-checking module
items.explanation: ChatGPT does not check facts — it predicts text. A false statement can sound just as plausible as a true one.
items.whyItMatters: This is the single most important limitation to understand.

items.question: ChatGPT gives you a legal citation. What should you do?
options: Trust it — ChatGPT is trained on legal documents
Verify the citation independently before using it
Ask ChatGPT again and see if it gives the same answer
Assume it is correct if it sounds reasonable
items.explanation: ChatGPT has hallucinated fake legal citations. Never use a citation without verification.
items.whyItMatters: This is a real-world case where verification prevents serious errors.

items.question: In your own words, why is ChatGPT more like a confident guesser than a database?
items.answer: Because ChatGPT generates text based on patterns, not facts. It produces the most likely response, which may or may not be true.
items.explanation: Understanding the mechanism explains the limitation. It also explains why ChatGPT is useful for drafting but dangerous for factual claims.
items.whyItMatters: This mental model guides how you use ChatGPT safely.

items.question: You asked ChatGPT for a summary of an article, and it wrote a statistic that you cannot find in the article. What most likely happened?
items.answer: ChatGPT hallucinated — it invented a plausible-sounding statistic that was not in the source. Always verify statistics against the original.
items.explanation: Summary tasks are especially prone to hallucination. The model may add plausible details that were not in the source.
items.whyItMatters: Verification is essential when ChatGPT summarizes sources you did not write yourself.

notes.summary: ChatGPT is a conversational AI powered by GPT models. It generates text based on patterns, not facts. This is why it hallucinates.
keyPoints: ChatGPT = conversational AI on GPT models
Generates text based on patterns — not database lookup
Verification is essential for factual claims
